On a distributed grid, the leftmost rank in a partitioned direction has topology
`RightConnected`. Its west/south boundary face (index 1) is a physical boundary,
but `periphery_offset(::Face, ::RightConnected, N)` returned 0, so `exclude_periphery`
launches stepped that face as if it were interior. This adds

    periphery_offset(::Face, ::RightConnected, N::Int) = ifelse(N > 1, 1, 0)

matching the treatment of `Bounded`.

Adds the MPI testset "Distributed open boundary faces are not stepped" to
`test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl`, which fails on `main` and passes with this change
(4 CPU ranks, x- and xy-partitions, QuasiAdamsBashforth2 and SplitRungeKutta3).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Exclude boundary face on RightConnected ranks from interior launches

body:
`BulkDrag` returns τ = −Cᴰ|U|u on every boundary. The domain-boundary `getbc` methods used the boundary side only to choose the index. Domain-boundary fluxes are positive in the +x, +y or +z direction, so `compute_z_top_bc!` (and the east/north versions) apply `G -= flux * A / V`. On those boundaries the drag therefore *added* Cᴰ|U|u·A/V to the tendency and sped the flow up. Bottom, west and south were correct. Immersed-boundary drag is unaffected, because immersed fluxes point into the fluid.

One forward-Euler step with `u = 1` (or `v = 1`), Cᴰ = 1e-3 and Δz = Δx = 0.25, before this PR:

```
bottom  u  Δ = -0.0040000000000000036
top     u  Δ = 0.0040000000000000036
west    v  Δ = -0.0040000000000000036
east    v  Δ = 0.0040000000000000036
```

This PR adds `boundary_sign(::LeftBoundary) = 1` and `boundary_sign(::RightBoundary) = -1` and multiplies the drag by it in the six domain-boundary `getbc` methods. Until now the tests covered only the bottom boundary. A new testset checks Δu = −Cᴰ U₀² Δt on all six boundaries. `test/time_stepping/bulk_drag.jl` passes on CPU and GPU.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Fix the sign of `BulkDrag` on top, east and north boundaries

body:
Quick follow-up to #6252. `materialize_mask` compares the mask's grid to the forced field's with `===` only, which rejects a mask built on a separately constructed but equal grid. 

**A common case** rather than an outlier: Breeze's `SpecificForcing` materializes its inner `Relaxation` against the *specific* field — `u`, `v`, `θ` out of its own field set — rather than the density-weighted prognostic it is keyed by, and that field's grid is `==` but not `===` to the grid a mask was built on. Measured on a nested child: `egal = false`, `equal = true`, locations matching. As it stands, every field-valued mask in that path throws at construction.

The tests in #6252 passed because they use a uniform `RectilinearGrid`, which is an immutable struct of isbits fields and therefore `===` to an identically constructed one. A grid that holds arrays is not, which is why the new case uses an array-backed grid.

Compare the way `AbstractOperations` already does for exactly this reason, `===` first so `==` does not synchronize the device for an immersed grid:

```julia
mask.grid === field.grid || mask.grid == field.grid ||
    throw(ArgumentError("a `Field` mask must share the forced field's grid"))
```

The existing rejection test uses a different-sized grid, so it still rejects.
title: Accept a `Relaxation` mask on an equal but distinct grid

The single-column parameter-estimation example manually traced its time-stepping loop and managed Enzyme derivative buffers. Use Reactant's `Simulation`/`run!` support and `Enzyme.gradient` instead, reset the model and clock before every evaluation, and give Optim a combined cost-and-gradient callback.

Keep the four-parameter BFGS fit and animation while removing the optimizer comparison, timing code, and duplicate iteration log. Shorten the explanations, simplify observation copies, use `on_architecture` for plotting data, and correct the dependency-installation and IFRT preference instructions. The example shrinks from 380 to 299 lines.

Validation on Julia 1.12.7 with Reactant 0.2.279, CPU/IFRT:

- Checked repeatability, the forward-run clock and iteration count, and agreement of all four gradients with finite differences (within 0.1%).
- Ran the 12-hour model and 10 BFGS iterations: cost fell from 0.108 to 0.000934; generated and inspected the plots and generated the animation.
- After the final shortening, verified that the numerical functions and animation were unchanged, tested all three Optim callback request modes, and generated the Literate Markdown.
- `git diff --check` passes.
title: Simplify the Reactant parameter estimation example
